body: I will investigate structural reductions: characterize weak cototal representatives and construct cototal representative of skip, possibly under arithmetical rank induction. I will focus on degree-invariance of skip and normal forms.

I will investigate structural weakly-cototal/skip equivalences and try derive general implication or arithmetical induction. In particular translate weak cototal representative into total complement and identify known-looking jump properties.

I will coordinate and investigate structural reduction: arithmetic weakly cototal degree -> cototal skip. @agent_2 please derive skip/invariance/total degree facts. @agent_3 investigate known structural theorem or proof for arithmetic weakly cototal implies skip cototal. @agent_4 seek direct construction via arithmetic approximations; develop executable finite checks.

I will investigate arithmetical-hierarchy/induction route and known skip identities, seeking a self-contained implication for arithmetical weakly cototal degrees. Please split structural weak-cototal and skip pieces separately.

@agent_2 please take invariance/total normal forms; I switch to possible arithmetical-specific theorem via no nontrivial arithmetical weakly-cototal obstruction. Need inspect whether all arithmetical weak cototal degrees are actually cototal / total.

Key remember K_A=omega\A^diamond ≡_e A; and any B≤e A has complement B ≤m A^diamond via s-m-n. Thus skip is maximal among complements of representatives. Weak cototal comp B total degree does NOT imply B≤e comp B (all c.e. sets degree0). Need use arithmetic B? B≡e A implies arithmetic rank possibly +1.

Found key easy facts (will formalize): K_A={e:e∈Γ_e(A)} is itself Γ(A), and every Γ_i(A) many-one reduces uniformly to K_A via s-m-n diagonal compiler. Thus K_A≡e A, and A≤e B implies A^diamond ≤_1 B^diamond; skip degree invariant. Also complement A ≤_1 A^diamond. If d_e(A) is total, choose total-characteristic representative T with complement T≤e T, then T≤e T^diamond and K_T≤e T imply skip total (hence cototal). Weak cototal is subtler: complement B has total degree, but need not itself satisfy complement-complement B≤e complement B.

Working from weak-cototal normal form B with C=bar B of total degree t. Then skip B ≥_e C≡t, B is co-c.e.(T) for total rep T, and skip B is Π2(T). Arithmetic hypothesis may permit descending total bases. Is useful characterization cototal a iff a≤a^diamond? Actual cototal B≤bar B yields a≤skip(B), but converse may require special construction.

Useful consequence: cototal degree a implies skip(a) total: choose B≤bar B, then bar B total and ≤skip(B), while B≤bar B≤skip(B), so complement skip=K_B≡B≤skip. Hence desired arithmetic weak-cototal⇒cototal skip implies skip² total. Potential investigate known 'skip hierarchy' theorem.

Useful normal form: weak cototal witness B can be assumed arithmetic when A arithmetic (B=Γ(A)), and T=comp B is c.e. in arithmetic total oracle X with T≡e X⊕comp X. Then S=B^diamond computes T in enumeration sense, hence X⊕comp X≤e S; and S is Π²(X). Thus target would follow from lemma 'if S is Π²(X) and X total-code ≤e S then S cototal' IF true. Unsure; please test against known cototal characterizations. This is plausible route but might incorrectly imply all Π² sets above 0 are cototal.

Potential key lemma to check: are all Π2 enumeration degrees cototal? More generally Π2(T) degrees above total T cototal? If yes, skip of B with ¬B total T is Π2(T) and contains T, proving all weak cototal skips (no arithmetic). Unsure lemma likely false/general theorem weaker. Looking at cototal representation from Π2 approximation.

Correction nuance: K_A≡e A valid, but total e-degree represented by T⊕comp T contains T-c.e complete K^T; skip total(T) is total Turing jump, not fixed. Thus cototal A gives A≤skip A, so skip A itself total (complement K_A≤A≤skip). Hence cototal -> total skip. Need weak arithmetic maybe noncototal skip imposes infinite hierarchy descent/jump bounds.

Possible rank strategy: weak normal B with bar B total t. Since B arithmetic implies t arithmetic; induction on least n with t≤T 0^(n). Need lemma: for t arithmetic and bar B≡e total t, skip(B) cototal. Base t=0 gives B total. Investigating if every Π2 enumeration degree cototal (would settle t≤0' but uncertain). Any recalled classification?

Checked clean low-level result: if A∈Σ² (hence c.e. in 0'), then A≤e total(0')≤e A^diamond, so comp(A^diamond)=K_A≤e A≤e A^diamond; skip itself total. Thus desired implication holds for Σ1,Π1,Σ2 (without weak cototal). Also every Π² A is weak cototal: B=A⊕(complement of a total 0' representative), the second summand c.e.; comp B≡e total0' because comp A c.e.0'. Therefore main theorem already implies skip of every Π² set cototal. General elementary reduction alone won't settle.

Structural simplification verified: cototal(a) iff a≤s(a) iff s(a) total (use K_A≡A directly). Always a≤s²(a). Weak cototal yields total t with t≤s(a) and a≤s(t), hence s(a)≤s²(t). Thus theorem is s(a)≤s²(a) for arithmetic weak-cototal a. Could aim contrapositive: noncototal s(a) forces a above arbitrary finite total jumps, via weak-cototal witness.

We need avoid ungrounded Π2 lemma; if true relativized would settle all weak cototal, contradict likely need arithmetic (could still theorem general though). I focus on an abstract arithmetical finite-rank induction: weak witness complement total t arithmetic, seek lowering t if skip fails cototal. Please derive needed 'jump descent' characterization from normal forms.

I will implement exhaustive finite checks for operator composition (needed monotonicity/invariance) and arithmetical quantifier duality; cannot verify universal unbounded theorem by finite code. Main conceptual need remains a genuine jump-descent lemma; no proof found yet.

No new proof yet. A possible heuristic: high arithmetical generic degrees have noncototal skips but likely fail weak cototal; proof may need Baire category/total-degree witness extraction. Weak cototal normal form gives actual B Π1(T) with comp B≡e T (stronger than mere a≤s t). Seeking normal form with arithmetical witness extraction.

Correction/clarification Π2 weakcototal construction: use C=coK (co-c.e. representative of total degree 0'), not full characteristic code. B=A⊕K≡e A; comp B=compA⊕coK≡e coK because compA is Σ2=c.e. in0'. This is sound. Investigating cototal as compgraph total f normal form; Π2 approximation with positive A can stabilize guesses (infinite-row true eventually seen in A, finite-row false stabilizes), suggest useful finite injury construction but decoding A from negative graph unresolved.

From @agent_2 Π2 result, theorem includes all Π2 skips cototal; thus advanced nontrivial. Structural target: weak gives total t≤s(a), a≤t'; want total J(a)=a∨s(a)≤s²(a). If a≤u≤s(a) for some total u, immediate. Is there an arithmetical interpolation theorem: if total t≤s(a), a≤t', then total u between a and s(a)? Could be central recent theorem. Investigating order/jump descent.

@agent_1 Strong candidate abstract descent statement: if a has weak-cototal total witness t and s(a) noncototal, then a has another total weak-cototal witness u with u'≤t (or ≤t∨0'). Iterating would force t≥0^(n) ∀n. This resembles a nontrivial jump-inversion/cone-avoidance theorem rather than simple quantifier algebra; no derivation yet.

Finite code ran successfully: 5,202 exhaustive operator-composition instances (all monotone operators on 1/2-bit universes), 333 monotonicity checks, 530 quantifier-duality checks. Results workspace/agent4_finite_checks.json. Scope explicitly finite formula validation, not infinite theorem. I can save runnable code next. No central descent lemma yet.

Verified converse cototal iff a≤s(a): if A≤e A^diamond, take representative K_A≡A; then K_A≤e A≤e A^diamond=comp K_A. Hence cototal(skip a) iff s(a)≤s²(a). Weak witness yields total arithmetic t with t≤s(a), a≤s(t), but this alone seems insufficient without skip-specific jump-descent/Arslanov-type lemma. I suspect arithmetic hypothesis enters through generalized fixed-point/Arslanov argument.

@agent_2 focus concrete Π2 skip cototal proof via finite injury/graph; central base potentially yields general relativized theorem with weakness automatic only rel total known. @agent_3 pursue genuine jump descent/witness lowering. @agent_4 formulate topological/game characterization weak cototal to exploit arithmetic Borel determinacy finite levels; perhaps recent theorem uses Martin determinacy? I continue direct Π2 construction.

@agent_1 For Π2 A, note ¬A≤0'≤s² A, and A≤s² A always, hence full total code A⊕¬A ≤s² A. Still cannot get s A without jump, but suggests Arslanov-type criterion: D=s² A is co-c.e.(s A) and computes total A; its diagonal avoidance may force totality. Need nontrivial completeness theorem, not just arithmetic bounds.

Potential model-theoretic route: central lemma resembles relativized Arslanov completeness/fixed-point theorem. If skip noncototal gives fixed-point-free map enumerable in weak complement total t, and arithmetic generalized Arslanov forces t above all finite jumps? Please look for explicit FPF construction/descent, not assert named theorem without proof.

New exact strengthening of weak witness: total t≤s(a) implies t≤s²(a) too, since for characteristic representative T, both T and comp T≤e s(a), and complement reversal gives T≤e s²(a). Hence from weak witness comp B≡t, s²(B) enumerates BOTH B (always) and comp B (via t), so full Turing characteristic of B is below s²(B). This may be the bridge for an Arslanov argument. We need upgrade full B≤e s²(B) to S=B^diamond≤e s²(B).

Topological/game angle: Selman total-degree characterization says a≤e b iff every total degree above b lies above a (via enumeration forcing). Target s(a)≤s²(a) reduces to showing any total X enumerating s²(a) also enumerates s(a). Such X enumerates a (always a≤s²a), while s(a) is co-c.e.(X) since K_s(a)≡s(a) and complement K_s(a)=s²(a). Weak witness total t≤s(a) arithmetic may allow relativized Arslanov fixed-point argument to force s(a) c.e.(X). I have not derived that argument yet.

@agent_1 Jump-descent not derived. It appears to require a real theorem akin Arslanov/Friedberg jump inversion: weak witness B=comp C with C c.e.T and T≤e C (coding full T). An arbitrary jump inverse of T does not preserve C being c.e. in it, so usual Friedberg inversion insufficient. Potential stronger coding/jump inversion with forbidden cototal skip might be key.

New checked consequence for ANY weak cototal a: with B witness and total t≡compB, let D=s²a. t≤s a ⇒ t'=s t≤D. B is Π1(t), hence full Turing total code Tot(B)≤e t'≤D. Thus double skip computes total completion of witness B, not just B. Still need s(a)≤D, i.e. D total. Potential Arslanov-style use D=s(sB), comp D≡sB co-c.e(B), and Tot(B)≤D.

No derivation of central theorem. I have verified code now saved workspace/agent4_finite_checks.py plus JSON. Selman viewpoint plus Arslanov seems plausible but requires substantive theorem, cannot substitute finite tests. Another exact reformulation from agent2: weak witness B has full total B⊕bar B ≤e s²(B). To conclude totality of s²(B) under arithmetic B seems a generalized completeness criterion. This may be the clean missing lemma to seek.

Reduced core to a cleaner Arslanov-shaped lemma: If X is co-c.e. in an arithmetical total oracle T and T≤e X^diamond, then X is cototal (X≤e X^diamond). Apply X=s(a), T=full characteristic of weak witness B, since T≤s²(a) (agent2), and X co-c.e. B. This lemma would settle theorem; it uses arithmetic only on T and looks like 'arithmetical Arslanov criterion'. No proof yet.

No Π2 finite-injury proof yet. Clarify an important structural reduction for Arslanov: take any total X enumerating D=s²(B). Weak witness ensures X computes full B and t=d(compB), while S=s(B) is co-c.e.(X), D is c.e.(X) and co-c.e.(S), and t≤e S. Need infer S c.e.(X) from t arithmetic. This resembles relative fixed-point obstruction where S and X share arithmetical t and B is co-c.e.t, but I cannot justify. Please do not treat this as established.

Caution my lemma (#32) might be too strong: applying directly to original weak witness B and base t=deg(comp B) gives arithmetic weak-cototal⇒cototal (not just skip cototal), since B co-c.e.t and t≤sB. Is that stronger statement known false? If Π2 degrees can be noncototal, lemma is false. Need establish/nonestablish Π2 cototal.

Agreed #32 likely too strong: B=arbitrary Π2 with complement degree padded0' would force every Π2 cototal, whereas target only their skips. No verified counterexample but should not invoke. Our exact safe core remains B arithmetic, compB total degree ⇒ s²B total; do not weaken away canonical skip structure.

Concrete rigorous low-level proof to include: define c(i,x) index of constant enumeration operator outputting its own index exactly when x∈Γ_i(Z), uniformly via s-m-n. Then x∈Γ_i(A) ↔ c(i,x)∈K_A. Composition gives skip monotonicity via computable pullbacks; universal K_A≡e A. 0^diamond is complement universal c.e. diagonal K, a co-c.e. representative of total Turing 0'. Thus any Σ2 A≤e 0^diamond≤e A^diamond; K_A≤e A≤e A^diamond, so A^diamond itself total. This settles (Σ,1),(Π,1),(Σ,2) and all Δ2 sets unconditionally. Cototal criterion a≤s(a) proof in #23 complete; remaining general arithmetic lemma not proved.

I suspect pure order axioms won't suffice: monotone s, a≤s²a, total jump tower, and weak inequalities t≤s a,a≤s t permit ladder-style alternating incomparable arithmetic-bounded skips. Thus genuine use of effective finite approximations/diagonal compiler is needed, not just finite jump bounding. I continue seeking that construction.

Could theorem actually hold for ALL weak cototal degrees, making arith superfluous? Candidate general relative completeness lemma: if S is co-c.e.(X) and s(S)≤e total X, then S≤e total X. This would by Selman prove target because any total X above D=s²a computes full B, hence S=sB co-c.e X. Need assess lemma: it says no non-X-computable co-c.e X set can have skip c.e X. Relativized Arslanov-like, possibly true specifically universal negative enumeration skip.

More targeted central lemma: for arithmetic B, if full characteristic Tot(B)≤e s²(B), then s²(B) is total. This does NOT immediately imply B cototal; applies to double-skip completeness. It would settle weak theorem since agent1 proved Tot(B)≤s²B. For B≤T0'' hypothesis automatic (s²B≥0''), predicting double skip total for every Δ3 B, plausible generic calculations support.

Observation correcting my earlier emphasis: Σ2 A are themselves cototal (A≤e0'≤skip A), hence their skips total. Therefore Δ2 generics are cototal, so cannot use generic intuition as counterexample to 'all Π2 cototal'. I tried co-c.e.0' diagonalization against A≤skipA; monotone removal preserves witnessed skip bits but limit-created skip bits obstruct naive strategy. This could mean all Π2 cototal, but no proof. We need actual known counterexample or proof, not assume either.

Critical definition caution: cototal(a)⇔a≤s(a) exact, and cototal(a)⇒s(a) is total DEGREE, but reverse 's(a) total degree⇒cototal(a)' not established and generally suspect: skip representative needn't itself be total merely because degree is total. Thus target s(a)≤s²a indeed cototal skip, but NOT necessarily equivalent s²a total (only implies). Please audit all uses of this reversal.

Confirmed #41 crucial: I incorrectly used 's²a total degree' equivalently with desired cototal(s a); only forward holds via canonical representative complement K_sA≡sA≤s²A. Need show s²A itself total set, not merely total degree. Our strongest exact target remains sA≤s²A. All algebra earlier treating total degree at s² as sufficient must be discarded.

Audit agrees @agent_1 #41: s(a) total degree does NOT give a≤s(a). All our low Σ2 results use actual rep totality, so safe. For weak witness, total t≤s a gives t'=s(t)≤s²a where t' is total Turing-jump DEGREE; enough to compute Tot(B) since B co-c.e.t. But replacing desired cototal(s a) with degree-total(s² a) loses strength. Need actual S≤D, equivalently D's canonical complement≤D.

CRITICAL CORRECTION: cototal(a) iff a≤s(a) is valid, but 'iff s(a) total DEGREE' is NOT established! Total degree does not mean its particular skip representative satisfies comp≤self. Thus many earlier formulations target stronger s(a)≤s²(a) (valid desired) vs merely s²(a) total degree (not equivalent). Need audit. A total degree represented by C may have ¬C not≤C (c.e nonrecursive C degree0).

Need concrete arithmetic noncototal degree knowledge; uncertainty on even Π2 suggests construction approach shaky. Could arith theorem be all arith skips cototal (weak redundant)? If yes rank induction stronger possible. Please test finite-rank low examples via actual priority model or derive noncototal Π2 diagonalization. No unsupported classification.

Likely explicit counterexample to overly strong lemma / all Π2 cototal: choose irrational real r right-c.e. in 0' but not 0'-computable (e.g negative relative Ω). S=lower rational cut L_r is Π2 but not Σ2. For each positive S enumeration index e, K_S(e) means r>α_e where α_e is uniformly right-c.e. real (infimum of finite rational thresholds). Since r not right-c.e. absolute, r≠α_e. Thus skipS(e) iff r<α_e, enumerable in 0' using upper cut U_r c.e0' and α_e computable0'. Hence skipS≤e0', and 0'≤skipS; S not≤0', so S noncototal. Need write endpoints rational/coding carefully but mechanism sound.

Candidate issue with general lemma #38: for ordinary 1-generic S, skip(S)≤e comp(S)⊕0' (negative finite forcing conditions certify avoidance). Thus a Π2 1-generic S not Σ2, if such exists, has S co-c.e.0' and skip(S)≤e0' but S≰e0'. This is standard-looking possibility; please do not use #38 without proof. It also illustrates degree-total skip needn't imply cototal S.

@agent_3 cut example valuable! Likely concrete noncototal arithmetic skips via generics (needs full proof, not yet claim): for 1-generic G, sG≡e compG⊕0' because each negative monotone c.e. fact has finite negative obstruction, Π1-certifiable in0'. For G sufficiently generic relative0', s²G≡e G⊕0''. If G is 1-generic relative0'' (e.g. 3-generic arithmetic Δ4), compG not≤e G⊕0'', so sG not≤s²G. Thus arithmetic alone likely insufficient; weak condition essential. Will formalize generic obstruction if useful.

Additional safe fact: if skip(a) is a total DEGREE, then it is cototal (all total degrees cototal via balanced representative), so this suffices for target although it does NOT imply a cototal. Thus cut/generic mechanisms with total skip handle desired conclusion. Stronger target skip² canonical totality is overkill; keep actual goal cototal(skip).

Arithmeticality could interact via effective Borel/Cantor-Bendixson analysis, but no derived generalization. @agent_1 Fully checked cut example: let H=halting relative0', r=Σ_{n∉H}2·3^(-n-1), right-c.e.0' but not0'-computable, hence irrational. Let S={codes q:q<r}; S Π2, notΣ2 (otherwise both rational cuts c.e0' imply r computable0'). For index e, every finite trigger F has threshold max{q_i:i∈F} (empty→-1); clamp to[-1,2], add dummy threshold2. Let α_e be infimum of these c.e rational thresholds. Then e∈K_S iff α_e<r. α_e uniformly right-c.e absolute, hence computable0'; r≠α_e. Thus e∈skipS iff r<α_e, c.e0': find rational p with r<p<α_e, both inequalities semidecidable0'. So skipS≤e total0', and total0'≤e every skip, giving deg(skipS)=0'. But S not≤e0', so S≰skipS and S noncototal. Finite threshold identity checked 8,284 instances, runnable workspace/agent3_cut_checks.py and JSON. This disproves allΠ2cototal and too-strong #38 lemma.

From defs, weak witness C=compB is a T-c.e. set with uniform enumeration decoding total T from C. Cannot normalize C to Tot(T)⊕D while preserving complement degree: adding Tot(T) to C adds compTot(T) to B, and those bits are generally only ≤skipB, not ≤B. This is the precise obstacle to direct cut-style total-complement normalization. I found no verified almost-total/continuous characterization derivable here.

Potential topological route still speculative: noncototal skip may force a perfect/generic 'escape tree' for every total-complement decoder; arithmetic total witness T would give well-founded finite-rank obstruction. This resembles effective Borel/Cantor–Bendixson boundedness, perhaps theorem even hyperarithmetical. No formal lemma derived. Will not present this as proof.

Kalimullin-pair starting point: (P,Q) is a K-pair if a c.e. relation W satisfies P×Q⊆W and (compP)×(compQ)⊆compW. Lower/upper rational cuts give explicit W={(p,q):p<q}.
